# What's this?
- Massachusetts utilities [publish](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/basic-service-information-and-rates#basic-service-pricing-) "Basic Service Pricing" sheets with monthly supply rates.
- We can use these for the supply portion of the bill
- This notebook is EDA for that sheet

# MA Electric Supply Rates
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(gt)
library(gtExtras)
library(jsonlite)
library(RSQLite)
library(readxl)
library(lubridate)

source("/workspaces/reports/lib/ggplot/switchbox_theme.R")

ma_supply_rates_monthly_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  path = "/workspaces/reports/data/utility_rates/electric/madpu/Basic Service Rates 12.30.2024.xlsx",
  sheet = "Monthly Prices",
  range = "A4:G255",
  .name_repair = "unique",  # Ensures column names are unique
  col_names = c("year", "month", "blank", "nationalgrid", "eversource_nstar", "eversource_wmeco", "unitil")
)

#View(ma_supply_rates_monthly_raw)

# Fill in missing year values by carrying forward the last valid year
ma_supply_rates_monthly <- ma_supply_rates_monthly_raw |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),  # Convert to numeric, invalid values become NA
    year = if_else(
      !is.na(year),  # If it's a valid year
      year,          # Keep it
      NA_real_      # Otherwise make it NA
    )
  ) |>
  fill(year, .direction = "down")|>  # Fill NAs with previous valid value
  mutate(
    month = case_when(
      month == "Jan" ~ 1,
      month == "Feb" ~ 2,
      month == "Mar" ~ 3,
      month == "Apr" ~ 4,
      month == "May" ~ 5,
      month == "June" ~ 6,
      month == "July" ~ 7,
      month == "Aug" ~ 8,
      month == "Sept" ~ 9,
      month == "Oct" ~ 10,
      month == "Nov" ~ 11,
      month == "Dec" ~ 12
    )
  ) |>
  select(-blank) |>
  mutate(
    eversource = (eversource_nstar + eversource_wmeco) / 2
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      -c(year, month),  # Select all columns except year and month
      ~ . / 100  # Divide each selected column by 100
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    type = "all_hours",
    zone = "everywhere"
  )

# Pivot to long format
ma_supply_rates_monthly_long <- ma_supply_rates_monthly |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(nationalgrid, eversource_nstar, eversource_wmeco, eversource, unitil),
    names_to = "electric_utility",
    values_to = "supply_rate"
  )

# Save to CSV
write.csv(
  ma_supply_rates_monthly_long,
  "/workspaces/reports/data/utility_rates/electric/madpu/ma_supply_rates_monthly_20250329.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

```


# Zero Muni Supply Rates
```{r}

# Get all unique month-year combinations
month_year_combinations <- ma_supply_rates_monthly_long |>
  distinct(year, month)

# Create municipal rows with supply_rate = 0
municipal_zeros <- month_year_combinations |>
  mutate(
    type = "all_hours",
    zone = "everywhere",
    electric_utility = "municipal",
    supply_rate = 0
  )

# Add these rows to the existing data - fix the variable name
ma_supply_rates_monthly_long <- bind_rows(
  ma_supply_rates_monthly_long,
  municipal_zeros
)

# Now view the correct dataframe
View(ma_supply_rates_monthly_long)

```

## Write to the DB
```{r}
# Write to database
path_rs_db <- "data/ResStock/2022_resstock_amy2018_release_1.1/rs_ma_hp_rates_2.db"
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), path_rs_db)
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "supply_rates_elec", ma_supply_rates_monthly_long, overwrite = TRUE)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

```


# Now use E3's rates database
## IOU rates
```{r }
#| label: data-ma-muni-supply-rates
path_ma_muni_supply_rates_xlsx <- "/workspaces/reports/data/utility_rates/electric/madpu/residential_electricity_rates_database_20250520.xlsx"


get_edc_supply_rates <- function(utility_name, component_subtype) {
  readxl::read_xlsx(
    path = path_ma_muni_supply_rates_xlsx,
    sheet = "Rates Database",
    range = "A2:L17583"
  ) |>
  filter(
    `Utility Type` == "Electric Distribution Company",
    `Component Subtype` == component_subtype,
    `Utility / Town Name` == utility_name,
    `Cost Category` == "Energy Supply"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = Year,
    month = as.integer(format(Month, "%m")),
    type = "all_hours",
    zone = "everywhere",
    electric_utility = `Utility / Town Name`,
    supply_rate = `$/kWh`
  ) |>
  select(
    year,
    month,
    type,
    zone,
    electric_utility,
    supply_rate
  )
}


ng_supply_rates <- get_edc_supply_rates("National Grid", "Basic Service Fixed Price")
eversource_wma_supply_rates <- get_edc_supply_rates("Eversource_WMA", "Basic Service Fixed Price")
eversource_ma_supply_rates <- get_edc_supply_rates("Eversource_EMA", "Basic Service Fixed Price")
unitil_supply_rates <- get_edc_supply_rates("Unitil", "Basic Service Fixed Price")

# ng_agg_supply_rates <- get_edc_supply_rates("National Grid", "Retail Aggregation Service Rate")
```

## Municipal rates
```{r }
path_ma_muni_supply_rates_xlsx <- "/workspaces/reports/data/utility_rates/electric/madpu/residential_electricity_rates_database_20250520.xlsx"

# Read the E3 rates data
muni_supply_rates <- readxl::read_xlsx(
  path = path_ma_muni_supply_rates_xlsx,
  sheet = "Rates Database",
  range = "A2:L17583"
) |>
filter(
  `Utility Type` == "Municipal Light Plant",
  `Cost Category` == "Energy Supply"
) |>
mutate(
  year = Year,
  month = as.integer(format(Month, "%m")),
  type = "all_hours",
  zone = "everywhere",
  muni_name = `Utility / Town Name`,
  supply_rate = `$/kWh`
) |>
select(
  year,
  month,
  type,
  zone,
  muni_name,
  supply_rate
)

#View(muni_supply_rates |> sample_n(20))

# Calculate median supply rates by year and month across all municipal utilities
muni_supply_rates_monthly <- muni_supply_rates |>
  group_by(year, month) |>
  summarise(
    supply_rate = median(supply_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    type = "all_hours",
    zone = "everywhere",
    electric_utility = "municipal"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Adding 2024 supply rates
#
# Remove any rows where year is 2024
muni_supply_rates_monthly_long <- muni_supply_rates_monthly |>
  filter(year != 2024)

inflation_202Y_to_2024 <- c(1.215, 1.16, 1.074, 1.032)
muni_supply_rates_2024 <- muni_supply_rates_monthly |>
  filter(year %in% c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023)) |>
  mutate(
    supply_rate = case_when(
      year == 2020 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[1],
      year == 2021 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[2],
      year == 2022 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[3],
      year == 2023 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[4],
      TRUE ~ supply_rate
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(
    supply_rate = mean(supply_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = 2024,
    type = "all_hours",
    zone = "everywhere",
    electric_utility = "municipal"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Adding 2023 Oct-Nov-Dec
#
# # Remove any rows where year is 2024
# muni_supply_rates_monthly_long <- muni_supply_rates_monthly |>
#   filter(year < 2023, month < 10)

inflation_202Y_to_2023 <- c(1.177, 1.124, 1.041, 1.0)
muni_supply_rates_Q4_2023 <- muni_supply_rates_monthly |>
  filter(year %in% c(2020, 2021, 2022)) |>
  filter(month %in% c(10, 11, 12)) |>
  mutate(
    supply_rate = case_when(
      year == 2020 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[1],
      year == 2021 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[2],
      year == 2022 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[3],
      year == 2023 ~ supply_rate * inflation_202Y_to_2024[4],
      TRUE ~ supply_rate
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(
    supply_rate = mean(supply_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = 2023,
    type = "all_hours",
    zone = "everywhere",
    electric_utility = "municipal"
  )

#View(muni_supply_rates_Q4_2023)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Append the 2024 data
muni_supply_rates_monthly <- bind_rows(
  muni_supply_rates_monthly,
  muni_supply_rates_2024,
  muni_supply_rates_Q4_2023
)

```



```{r}
supply_rates_monthly_long <- bind_rows(
  muni_supply_rates_monthly,
  ma_supply_rates_monthly_long,
  ng_supply_rates,
  eversource_wma_supply_rates,
  eversource_ma_supply_rates,
  unitil_supply_rates
)

# Create datetime column and plot supply rates
supply_rates_monthly_long |>
  filter(electric_utility != "municipal") |>
  filter(year > 2016) |>
  #filter(electric_utility %in% c("municipal", "nationalgrid", "eversource", "unitil")) |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, "01", sep = "-")),
    electric_utility = factor(electric_utility)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = supply_rate, color = electric_utility)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  labs(
    title = "Massachusetts Electric Supply Rates",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Supply Rate ($/kWh)",
    color = "Utility"
  )

```


```{r}

supply_rates_plot <- supply_rates_monthly_long |>
  filter((year > 2015) & (year < 2024)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = electric_utility, values_from = supply_rate, values_fill = 0) |>
  select(year, month, eversource, nationalgrid, unitil, municipal) |>
  mutate(
    muni_over_eversource = municipal/eversource,
    muni_over_nationalgrid = municipal/nationalgrid,
    muni_over_unitil = municipal/unitil
  ) |>
  select(
    month,
    muni_over_eversource,
    muni_over_nationalgrid,
    muni_over_unitil
  ) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarize(
    muni_over_eversource = mean(muni_over_eversource),
    muni_over_nationalgrid = mean(muni_over_nationalgrid),
    muni_over_unitil = mean(muni_over_unitil),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

View(supply_rates_plot)
```

# 12-month spaghetti plot
```{r}


muni_supply <- muni_supply_rates |>
  mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01"))
  )



mean_muni_rates <- muni_supply |>
  group_by(year, month, type, zone) |>
  summarise(
    supply_rate = mean(supply_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    muni_name = "mean_muni",
    date = lubridate::ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01"))
  )

median_muni_rates <- muni_supply |>
  group_by(year, month, type, zone) |>
  summarise(
    supply_rate = median(supply_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    muni_name = "median_muni",
    date = lubridate::ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01"))
  )

# Bind the mean rates to the original data
muni_supply_x <- bind_rows(
  muni_supply,
  mean_muni_rates,
  median_muni_rates
)

#View(muni_supply_x)




# Create time series plot for each unique municipal utility
muni_supply_x |>
  mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = supply_rate, color = muni_name, group = muni_name)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  labs(
    title = "Massachusetts Municipal Utilities Electric Supply Rates",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Supply Rate ($/kWh)",
    color = "Municipal Utility"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")  # Hiding legend due to many municipalities





  ```
